summary: The audit checks the 45 graduate units and the three core courses, GERMAN 330, 331 and 332. The rest of the 45 units must be graduate-level GERMAN courses (numbered 200 or above) or approved courses in related fields such as art history, comparative literature, linguistics, history or philosophy; you add approved related-field courses by hand. The oral examination on your 45-text reading list is checked by hand.

vGUKbrs9.why: "students must complete a minimum of 45 units of graduate work" and "The student may select the remaining courses, but they must be graduate-level courses in German and/or approved courses in related fields": the 45 units are the core courses, graduate-level GERMAN courses and approved related-field courses, so they are counted over this block rather than over every graduate course on the record.

zJF971bk.why: "To complete the MA degree, students must complete a minimum of 45 units of graduate work" is the program's minimum; the rest describes the coterminal option.

NLEBNjaJ.why: "The MA program requires students to take the three graduate core courses (GERMAN330, GERMAN331, and GERMAN332)" is the Required Courses rule. "The student may select the remaining courses, but they must be graduate-level courses in German and/or approved courses in related fields such as art history, comparative literature, linguistics, history, or philosophy." "MA candidates must take an oral examination toward the end of their last quarter ... students are expected to compile a reading list of 45 texts". The remaining courses have no count of their own; the block's 45-unit floor counts them. Graduate level is courses numbered 200 and above: many graduate GERMAN listings (GERMAN 230, 231, 232) carry no graduate-career tag.
